docs.title: ZamLine Technical Documentation
docs.text:
ZamLine brings shipment opportunities, fleet requirements, route information and operating-cost estimates into one workflow for verified Shippers and Fleet Managers in Zambia.

Start with the problem Explore the architecture

docs.title: What ZamLine does
docs.text:
Zambia's road freight depends on manual trip planning and costing, and available truck capacity is not always used well. ZamLine connects the two sides of that problem. Shippers publish loads. Fleet Managers see the loads their trucks can carry, review route and cost information, and decide whether to accept. The first valid acceptance reserves the load for one fleet company and releases contact details between the two businesses.

Read the full problem statement

docs.title: AI Module
docs.text:
The AI module estimates the cost of a journey so a Fleet Manager can compare it with the Shipper's proposed payment. It gets route distance and duration from the routing service, then asks the Gemini API for a cost estimate and explanation, using Markdown reference files as background. The result fills the cost fields, estimated_margin, outcome and ai_explanation on shipment_matches.

Page What it covers Reference data How the reference files are produced from source documents and datasets Security and privacy What data reaches Gemini, key handling, output boundaries Testing and evaluation Required tests and the state of evaluation evidence Deployment and operations Reference-file storage, Gemini file expiry and refresh, production operations

docs.title: Inputs, outputs and model
docs.text:
Item Detail Route inputs Route distance and duration from the routing service Fleet inputs From companies: fuel price, driver allowance, toll assumption, other costs. From trucks: fuel consumption and maintenance per km. Shipment input The shipment's proposed amount Background The Markdown reference files Outputs Cost fields, estimated_total_cost, estimated_margin, outcome and ai_explanation on shipment_matches Model access The model is called through the Gemini API. No training or fine-tuning is described. Failure estimated_total_cost is null when the AI call fails

The Gemini model name and version, the prompt, and the response format are not specified in the project material and are therefore not documented here.

docs.title: What the Fleet Manager sees
docs.text: The cost estimation screen shows the journey, a calculated operating cost, and the AI freight estimate next to the Shipper's proposed payment.

docs.title: Interpreting estimates
docs.text:
ZamLine is decision support, and the Fleet Manager makes the accept or decline decision. Treat estimates as indicative, not as guaranteed costs or profit.

Boundary Statement AI-generated content ai_explanation is written by the model. Deterministic logic The compatibility filter, the margin subtraction (proposed_amount minus estimated_total_cost) and reservation uniqueness are application logic, not model output. Human decision Accepting or declining is done by the Fleet Manager. Empty estimate The estimate is empty when the AI call fails. A failed or incomplete result is never presented as a successful estimate. Reference data The reference data is historical and partial.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Responsibility manifest.json Lists the reference files used by the backend upload workflow Reference-file upload workflow Uploads the reference files to the Gemini Files API and maintains usable file references Gemini API key Retrieved by the backend from the Vault or secret manager Reference documents Curated Markdown files produced by the reference-data notebook

docs.title: Operating the reference files
docs.text:
1. Run the notebook when source documents change, and review quality_report.csv.
  2. Place the resulting Markdown files and manifest.json in server-side storage with access restricted to authorised services.
  3. The backend checks file references before use and refreshes expired Gemini file references.
  4. Keep API keys and file-registry details out of client responses and application logs.
  5. Keep the manifest and source documents under version control or controlled release storage so updates are traceable.

docs.title: Gemini file expiry and refresh
docs.text:
Files uploaded through the Gemini Files API are not stored permanently, so the backend manages their availability.

Storage

  • Original Markdown files stay in persistent server-side storage.
  • The Gemini file reference and upload timestamp for each file are kept in a local JSON configuration file on the application server.

Before each use

  1. The backend checks whether the file's uploaded reference is still valid.
  2. If it has expired or is no longer available, the backend re-uploads the original Markdown file.
  3. After every successful upload, the backend replaces the stored reference and upload timestamp.
  4. Later Gemini requests use the new reference.

docs.title: Production operations
docs.text:
• Protect shared reference-file storage with least-privilege access.
  • Make refresh operations safe to retry, and prevent concurrent refreshes from creating a conflicting registry.
  • Deploy reference updates through a controlled release so active estimates use a consistent reference set.
  • Monitor provider failures, expired file references, upload failures and estimate completion errors.
  • Return a controlled failure when required reference files cannot be loaded. Do not present an incomplete estimate as successful.

docs.title: Reference data
docs.text: Cost estimation uses Markdown reference files as background. The notebook zamline_reference_files generates them from source documents and structured datasets. The notebook, the source documents and the datasets are not part of this documentation repository; this page describes how the notebook is documented to work.

docs.title: What the notebook produces
docs.text: It writes one Markdown file per source document, with a source header and ## Page N markers so extracted information can be traced to the corresponding PDF page. It also writes Markdown summaries for five structured datasets. The original CSV files are not changed.

docs.title: Notebook steps
docs.text:
1. Read the source list zamline_core_sources.csv and match each source to its PDF in 01_Raw_Documents. Sources without a PDF are reported as missing and are not replaced with other copies.
  2. Skip exact duplicate PDFs using a SHA-256 checksum, and flag unreadable PDFs.
  3. Extract text page by page. OCR (Tesseract, at 220 DPI) runs only on pages with fewer than 200 characters of text. OCR output replaces the text layer only when it adds text with a mean confidence of at least 60.
  4. Clean the text. A line is removed only if it is a page label, a page number at the top or bottom of a page, or a header or footer repeated on at least 40 percent of pages. Hyphenated words and broken lines are rejoined. Wording and numbers are not changed. Numbers are counted before and after cleaning so that any lost figure appears in the quality report.
  5. Write one .md file per document.
  6. Validate the structured datasets (size, missing values, duplicate rows) and write short summaries.
  7. Write the manifest and quality reports.

docs.title: Structured datasets
docs.text:
The notebook lists D01, D02, D04, D05 and D06. There is no D03.

ID File Notes D01 SCMS_Raw_Global_Shipment_History_10324_Rows.csv Raw export D02 SCMS_Cleaned_African_Truck_Freight_1160_Rows.csv Truck shipments only, with positive freight cost and weight. Checked against D01. docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
The notebook writes to the folder ZamLine_Data_Review/reference_files.

File Purpose One .md per document and per structured summary The files uploaded to the Gemini Files API manifest.json Lists every reference file with source details, for the backend upload script manifest.csv The same data for spreadsheet review quality_report.csv Per-document warnings structured_validation.csv Dataset checks

Quality warnings are: PDF missing, very short, OCR used, mostly graphics, and numbers lost. The "numbers lost" warning should never appear.

docs.title: Running the notebook
docs.text:
• Prerequisites: the Python packages pymupdf, pytesseract, Pillow, pandas and tabulate (the first cell installs any that are missing), and the Tesseract binary. In Colab the Tesseract install is automatic. Elsewhere, install it yourself, otherwise pages that need OCR are flagged.
  • Folder layout: a ZamLine_Data folder containing zamline_core_sources.csv, 01_Raw_Documents and 06_Structured_Data. In Colab it is read from /content/drive/MyDrive/ZamLine_Data. Locally, the project root is the current folder, or its parent when the current folder is named ZamLine_Data_Review.
  • Settings: only the Settings cell should need editing (paths, MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE, OCR_DPI, OCR_MIN_CONFIDENCE, document notes, dataset file names).
  • Run: execute all cells from top to bottom. The OCR step takes several minutes.
  • Verify: check the warnings column of the quality report and spot-check a cleaned document. The notebook defaults to DOC018.

docs.title: AI security and privacy
docs.text: This page covers the Gemini cost estimator, the Markdown reference files and the Gemini file registry. Routing-service security is in Backend security.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Area Requirement Data sent to Gemini Structured context only, with content filtering. This includes journey details and fleet cost inputs, as listed in Inputs, outputs and model. Only the minimum context required for the estimate is shared. Gemini API key Stored as a server-side secret, fetched only by authorised backend services and never sent to the client. Private cost data Fleet cost settings are high-sensitivity data and remain organisation-scoped. How this data is handled when used by Gemini is not detailed in the project material. Model-version traceability The model version should be recorded with cost-prediction inputs and outputs. How it is recorded is not documented. Failure behaviour If a re-upload of a reference file fails, the backend reports the failure and does not use an invalid reference.

docs.title: Threats
docs.text: Threat Component Required control Incorrect cost calculation Cost assessment Validated inputs, transparent assumptions, independently verified calculation tests Exposure of private cost information Cost assessment, database Organisation isolation, authorization, minimum necessary exposure Private data reaching a third party beyond what the estimate needs Gemini integration Structured context only, content filtering, minimum necessary data

docs.title: Boundaries of the output
docs.text:
• The estimate is decision support. The Fleet Manager decides.
  • Cost results are meant to be deterministic and independently verifiable, while the explanation is generated by a model. The estimate must not be presented as a guaranteed cost or profit.
  • Reference data is historical and partial.

docs.title: State of the evidence
docs.text:
No evaluation dataset, metrics, baseline or results for the cost estimate are included in the project material, so this documentation states no accuracy figures. Do not describe the estimate as accurate or reliable without evaluation results. Until such results exist, treat estimates as indicative decision support.

An evaluation of the cost estimate would need an evaluation dataset of journeys with known costs, metrics and a baseline to compare against, results by journey type, and known failure cases. Add the artefacts and their results here when they exist.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
These tests come from ZamLine's security requirements.

Test What it checks Cost-calculation verification Deterministic cost results match independently calculated expected values External API failure The system handles unavailable services, authentication failures and invalid input Source code review Review of the cost-handling logic

docs.title: Recommended behaviour tests
docs.text: Behaviour Expected result AI call fails estimated_total_cost is null, no stale value is displayed, and the request reports failure Margin arithmetic estimated_margin equals proposed_amount minus estimated_total_cost File expiry An expired Gemini reference triggers a re-upload and updates the registry Failed re-upload The failure is reported and the invalid reference is not used Concurrent re-upload Refresh operations are coordinated so concurrent requests keep a valid registry and never expose conflicting references

docs.title: Reference-data quality checks
docs.text:
The reference-data notebook has built-in checks. They validate the preparation of the data, not the quality of the estimates.

Check How it works Missing or duplicate sources Missing PDFs are reported, and duplicate files are skipped using SHA-256 hashes Text extraction OCR is used only for pages with fewer than 200 characters, and accepted at a mean confidence of 60 or above No lost numbers Numbers are counted before and after cleaning, and any loss is recorded in quality_report.csv Dataset validation Size, missing values and duplicate rows are recorded in structured_validation.csv Spot check A cleaned document is reviewed, with DOC018 used by default

See also Backend testing and Frontend testing.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
ZamLine is a Progressive Web App (PWA) in front of a backend API. The backend is organised into modules (authentication, business verification, shipments, fleet management, fleet matching, cost estimation, allocation and contact handoff) and stores its data in PostgreSQL. Two external services support cost estimation: a routing service for distance and duration, and the Gemini API for the cost explanation.

Page What it covers This page The two architecture diagrams and the decisions that shape the design Components and responsibilities What each component does, layer by layer Data flow and external services How requests, verification, cost estimates and allocation move through the system

docs.title: System architecture
docs.text: The diagram below shows the application modules and how the two user roles reach them through the PWA. Each module reads and writes application data through the backend API. The Cost Estimation module calls the routing service and the Gemini Files API, and uses Markdown reference files for background.

docs.title: Secure architecture
docs.text: The second diagram groups the same system into five layers: users and devices, perimeter security, the application layer, the data layer and external services. Traffic enters over HTTPS and passes DNS and DDoS protection, a web application firewall (WAF) and an API gateway before it reaches the backend. The diagram labels the WAF as provided by Vercel and the encrypted backup storage as Supabase.

docs.title: Architectural decisions
docs.text: Decision Description Progressive Web App One PWA serves both Shippers and Fleet Managers. Layered security perimeter DNS and DDoS protection, a WAF and an API gateway filter traffic before it reaches the backend. Backend as the authority The backend enforces authentication, authorization, validation and audit logging. The browser is never trusted for permissions or cost privacy. Secret management Credentials and application secrets are held in a secret manager (Vault), not in source code or client configuration. Single-winner allocation A uniqueness constraint on reservations.shipment_id and an atomic backend check prevent a shipment from being allocated twice. Private fleet cost data Fleet cost settings are scoped to the organisation that owns them. Delayed contact handoff Contact details are released only after a valid reservation. Reference files for cost estimation Markdown reference files are uploaded to the Gemini Files API. Because uploaded files expire, the backend keeps the originals and re-uploads them when needed. See AI operations.

docs.title: Components and responsibilities
docs.text: Components are grouped by the layers of the secure architecture diagram.

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Component Responsibilities Shipper (PWA) Registers and submits the PACRA certificate, posts shipments, views shipment status and allocation, receives the fleet company's contact details after allocation. Fleet Manager (PWA) Manages trucks, availability and private cost settings, views eligible shipments and cost assessments, accepts or declines shipments, receives the shipper's contact details after allocation.

docs.title: Perimeter
docs.text: Component Responsibilities DNS and DDoS protection DDoS mitigation and rate limiting. WAF Input and output sanitisation, bot blocking and rate limiting. Labelled as provided by Vercel in the secure architecture diagram. API gateway Request schema and body-size validation, rate and abuse controls, login and OTP throttling, security headers.

docs.title: Application (backend)
docs.text: Component Responsibilities Authentication and OTP Email and password login, short-lived single-use email OTP, attempt and resend limits, session after OTP verification. Authorization Role enforcement, organisation scope, object and ownership checks. Business verification PACRA certificate validation using QR and OCR checks. Fails safely when information cannot be reliably processed. See Business verification. Shipment management Creates and validates shipments. The Shipper confirms before publication. Cargo validation Rejects cargo types that ZamLine does not accept. Fleet management Fleet records, truck capacity, body type and availability. Fleet matching Selects open shipments that an available truck can carry. Cost estimation Route distance and duration, private organisation-scoped cost inputs, comparison of the shipment's proposed payment with the estimated cost. See AI Module. First-accept allocation Backend state check and an atomic guard against double allocation. Contact handoff Releases relevant contacts only after successful allocation.

docs.title: Data and storage
docs.text: Component Responsibilities PostgreSQL (encrypted) Accounts, organisations, fleet, shipments, cargo, matches, reservations, private costs and audit records. See Data model. Certificate storage Holds PACRA certificate files separately from the database. The database stores a reference (companies.certificate_file_url). Reference file storage Holds the Markdown reference files used by cost estimation. Gemini file registry A local JSON configuration file on the application server that records each Gemini file reference and its upload timestamp. Secret manager (Vault) Database credentials, routing and email credentials, application secrets. Audit and security logs Authentication, OTP, authorization, verification, cargo and allocation events. Passwords, OTPs and API keys are excluded. Encrypted backups Backup storage on Supabase with restricted backup access and separate recovery access.

docs.title: External services
docs.text: Service Responsibilities Openrouteservice Route distance, duration and route details using the heavy-goods-vehicle profile. Gemini API Generates the cost-estimate explanation from structured context and the uploaded reference files. Content filtering applies.

docs.title: Main flows
docs.text: Flow Path Request PWA → HTTPS/TLS → DNS and DDoS protection → WAF → API gateway → backend module → PostgreSQL Verification A Shipper or Fleet Manager uploads a PACRA certificate → business verification (QR and OCR) → verification_status on companies. Every attempt is written to audit_logs. Cost estimate Backend → routing service (distance, duration) and Gemini API (reference files and journey details) → cost fields on shipment_matches Allocation Acceptance → backend state check → atomic guard → reservations row → shipment confirmed → other matches for the shipment closed Contact handoff After allocation only: the Shipper sees the accepting company's permitted contacts, and contact_viewed is logged. Reference file refresh The backend checks the Gemini file reference, re-uploads the Markdown original if it has expired, and updates the local registry. See Gemini file expiry and refresh.

docs.title: External services
docs.text: Service Purpose Data shared Credential handling Openrouteservice Distance and duration for the route Origin and destination coordinates and routing parameters API key in the Vault, fetched only by the backend, never exposed to the PWA, source code or logs Gemini API Cost estimate and explanation Structured context only, with content filtering API key held as a server-side secret Supabase Encrypted backups Backup copies of application data Restricted backup access and separate recovery access Email provider Delivery of OTP emails Recipient address and one-time code Credentials in the Vault. The provider is not named in the project material.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
The ZamLine backend is the trusted service layer between the Progressive Web App, PostgreSQL, business-verification processing, the routing service and AI cost estimation. It owns authentication, authorization, validation, data integrity and audit events. The browser is never the authority for permissions or cost privacy.

Page What it covers Data model Tables, columns, constraints and relationships Business verification PACRA certificate upload, QR and OCR checks, verification outcomes Security Authentication, authorization, validation, allocation integrity, logging Testing Required and recommended backend tests Deployment Hosting and release requirements

docs.title: API design
docs.text:
The API is organised around the resource families below. All protected operations require authentication and server-side authorization. Route paths, HTTP methods and payload schemas are not listed in this documentation; the table describes the operations each family is designed to support.

Resource family Typical operations Authorization rule Authentication Register, log in, verify OTP, resend OTP, log out, retrieve the current account Public only where needed for account creation and authentication. OTP endpoints are rate-limited. Companies Read and update the own business profile, submit or retrieve verification status Company owner or authorized member. Certificate access is restricted. Fleet and trucks List, create, update and deactivate trucks, maintain operating-cost settings Fleet Manager within the owning company Shipments Create, publish, list eligible shipments, retrieve details, update or cancel permitted states The Shipper owns mutations. Fleet Managers see eligible published opportunities. Matches and assessments Retrieve compatible shipments, request or retrieve route and cost assessment Fleet Managers see only permitted estimate fields. Private inputs stay organisation-scoped. Reservations Accept or decline a shipment, retrieve reservation and allocation state Eligible Fleet Manager. Acceptance is atomic and single-winner. Contact handoff Retrieve counterparty business contact details after allocation Only the parties entitled under the successful reservation Audit events Record and inspect audit data Writes from trusted services. Reads restricted to authorized operators.

docs.title: Business rules
docs.text:
• Only verified businesses take part in protected shipper and fleet workflows.
  • Only published, open shipments are considered for matching.
  • Only available trucks that meet the shipment's requirements are eligible.
  • Private company operating-cost settings and private truck cost fields are visible only to the owning fleet company and the backend's assessment logic.
  • A Shipper's proposed payment is commercially sensitive data.
  • Accepting a shipment is transactional: it cannot be allocated to more than one Fleet Manager.
  • Contact handoff follows a successful reservation and is audit logged.
  • Invalid weights, negative payments, impossible capacity values and invalid route inputs are rejected on the server.

docs.title: Response and error conventions
docs.text:
Successful responses return structured JSON. Validation errors identify the invalid field without echoing sensitive input. Authorization failures do not reveal whether another organisation's private record exists. A state conflict, such as a shipment that was already allocated, returns a conflict response so the frontend can refresh its state. Failures of the routing service or the AI call return controlled errors without provider credentials, stack traces or internal details.

Responses should carry a request or correlation identifier for tracing. Logs must exclude passwords, OTP values, access tokens, API keys and unnecessary personal or commercial data.

docs.title: Audit events
docs.text: The audit trail covers authentication events, verification attempts and outcomes, shipment publication and material changes, shipment views where required, fleet changes, cost-assessment requests, allocation outcomes, contact handoff and authorization failures. Each event records a timestamp, the actor and organisation where applicable, an action type, a reference to the target record, the outcome and a minimal details object. The table is described in Data model.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
The database has seven tables: companies, users, trucks, shipments, shipment_matches, reservations and audit_logs. PostgreSQL is the database.

In the tables below, Req is R for required and O for optional. Columns that accept a fixed set of values are stored as VARCHAR in the database; the permitted values are listed in the Constraints column.

docs.title: companies
docs.text:
Business profile for shippers and fleet companies, the latest PACRA verification result, and for fleet companies only, private cost settings. Cost columns are NULL for shippers and must be returned only to users of the same company. Only the latest verification result is kept here; every attempt is kept in audit_logs.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description company_id UUID R PK System generated identifier. company_type VARCHAR R shipper or fleet Shipper posts freight; fleet owns trucks and accepts freight. business_name VARCHAR(100) R Registered business name entered at sign-up. registration_number VARCHAR(20) R UNIQUE PACRA registration number. Prevents duplicate registration. company_email VARCHAR(255) R UNIQUE Official company email. phone_number VARCHAR(15) R Shared with the other party only after a valid reservation. verification_status VARCHAR R DEFAULT pending; pending, verified, resubmit, rejected Controls whether the company can post or accept shipments. resubmit means data is missing, unreadable or mismatched. verified_at TIMESTAMP O When the company became verified. Used for activation metrics. certificate_file_url VARCHAR(255) O Storage link to the latest uploaded certificate. verification_failure_reason TEXT O Reason the last attempt failed, for example QR not found or name mismatch. fuel_price_per_litre DECIMAL(10,2) O CHECK > 0 Fleet only. Fuel price used in estimates. driver_daily_allowance DECIMAL(10,2) O Fleet only. Daily driver allowance. toll_assumption DECIMAL(10,2) O DEFAULT 0 Fleet only. Expected toll cost per trip. other_costs DECIMAL(10,2) O DEFAULT 0 Fleet only. Other operating cost per trip. currency CHAR(3) O Three-character currency code. created_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() Record creation time. updated_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() Last change time.

docs.title: users
docs.text:
Login details. A user always belongs to one company, which keeps each company's data separate. Data comes from the registration form.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description user_id UUID R PK System generated identifier. company_id UUID R FK to companies.company_id The user's company. first_name VARCHAR(50) R First name. last_name VARCHAR(50) R Last name. email VARCHAR(255) R UNIQUE Login email. password_hash VARCHAR R Password hash used for email and password login. role VARCHAR R shipper or fleet_manager Decides which screens and actions the user can access. is_active BOOLEAN R DEFAULT TRUE Whether the account can log in. created_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() Account creation time.

docs.title: trucks
docs.text:
Trucks owned by fleet companies. Body type, capacity and availability drive the compatibility filter. Fuel use and maintenance cost are stored per truck because they differ between vehicles. Data comes from the fleet setup screen.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description truck_id UUID R PK Identifier. company_id UUID R FK to companies.company_id Owning fleet company. plate_number VARCHAR(20) R UNIQUE Number plate. Blocks duplicates. truck_type VARCHAR(30) R Category, for example rigid or semi-trailer. body_type VARCHAR R flatbed, box, tanker, refrigerated, tipper, container Compared with the shipment's required_body_type. capacity_kg FLOAT R CHECK > 0 Maximum load in kg. Compared with the shipment's weight_kg. fuel_consumption_l_per_100km FLOAT R CHECK > 0 Private. Average fuel use per 100 km. maintenance_per_km DECIMAL(10,2) R Private. Maintenance cost per km. availability_status VARCHAR R DEFAULT available; available, unavailable Only available trucks are used for matching. Changed manually by the fleet manager. current_location VARCHAR(50) O Town or place where the truck is available. available_from TIMESTAMP O When the truck becomes free. created_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() When the truck was added. updated_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() Last change time.

docs.title: shipments
docs.text:
Freight opportunities posted by shippers: route, cargo, pickup time and proposed payment. Only open shipments appear to fleet managers.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description shipment_id UUID R PK Identifier. company_id UUID R FK to companies.company_id Shipper company that posted it. user_id UUID R FK to users.user_id User who created it. origin_address VARCHAR(250) R Pickup location as text. origin_latitude NUMERIC(9,6) R CHECK -90 to 90 Pickup latitude. origin_longitude NUMERIC(9,6) R CHECK -180 to 180 Pickup longitude. destination_address VARCHAR(250) R Delivery location as text. destination_latitude NUMERIC(9,6) R CHECK -90 to 90 Delivery latitude. destination_longitude NUMERIC(9,6) R CHECK -180 to 180 Delivery longitude. cargo_type VARCHAR(20) R Kind of cargo, for example maize or copper cathode. weight_kg FLOAT R CHECK > 0 Cargo weight in kg. required_body_type VARCHAR R flatbed, box, tanker, refrigerated, tipper, container Truck body type the cargo needs. Validated against the supported truck body-type values. pickup_time TIMESTAMP R Earliest pickup time. special_requirements TEXT O Extra notes such as permits or handling needs. proposed_amount DECIMAL(12,2) R CHECK > 0 Amount the shipper is willing to pay. status VARCHAR R DEFAULT open; open, confirmed, cancelled, expired Lifecycle. Becomes confirmed when a fleet manager accepts. published_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() When the shipment became visible.

docs.title: shipment_matches
docs.text:
Possible matches between a shipment and a compatible truck. Holds the route, the cost estimate and the fleet manager's decision. A shipment and truck pair can appear only once.

Table-level constraint: UNIQUE (shipment_id, truck_id).

The decided_at column is part of the data model specification but does not appear in the schema export.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description match_id UUID R PK Identifier. shipment_id UUID R FK to shipments.shipment_id Matched shipment. truck_id UUID R FK to trucks.truck_id Matched truck. user_id UUID O FK to users.user_id Fleet manager who made the decision. distance_km FLOAT O Route distance. Empty until the manager selects the match. duration INTEGER O Estimated journey time in minutes. fuel_cost DECIMAL(12,2) O Estimated fuel cost. driver_cost DECIMAL(12,2) O Estimated driver cost. toll_cost DECIMAL(12,2) O Estimated toll cost. maintenance_cost DECIMAL(12,2) O Estimated maintenance cost. other_cost DECIMAL(12,2) O Other estimated costs. estimated_total_cost DECIMAL(12,2) O Estimated total journey cost. Empty if the AI call failed. proposed_amount DECIMAL(12,2) O Shipper's proposed payment at the time of the estimate. estimated_margin DECIMAL(12,2) O proposed_amount minus estimated_total_cost. outcome VARCHAR O profit, loss, break_even Financial category of the margin. The cost-estimation logic applies the thresholds; they are not specified here. ai_explanation TEXT O Written explanation of the main factors behind the estimate. manager_decision VARCHAR R DEFAULT pending; pending, accepted, declined, closed closed is set when another company secures the shipment first. Accepted and declined are both stored. created_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() Match creation time. decided_at TIMESTAMP O When the manager decided.

docs.title: reservations
docs.text:
Records which fleet company secured a shipment. Created only at the moment of a valid acceptance, so no row exists while a shipment is waiting. The unique constraint on shipment_id means two companies can never claim the same load.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description reservation_id UUID R PK Identifier. shipment_id UUID R FK to shipments.shipment_id, UNIQUE One reservation per shipment. company_id UUID R FK to companies.company_id Fleet company that secured the shipment. truck_id UUID R FK to trucks.truck_id Truck assigned. user_id UUID R FK to users.user_id Fleet manager who accepted. match_id UUID R FK to shipment_matches.match_id The accepted match with its cost estimate. status VARCHAR R accepted, cancelled accepted when created; cancelled if the arrangement is later called off. reserved_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() When the shipment was secured.

docs.title: audit_logs
docs.text:
General log of user actions such as viewing, assessing, accepting and publishing. Written by the backend API for every module. See Audit events.

Column SQL type Req Constraints Description audit_id UUID R PK Identifier. user_id UUID O FK to users.user_id User who did the action. company_id UUID O FK to companies.company_id Company of the user. action_type VARCHAR(50) R Action name, for example shipment_published, shipment_viewed, verification_attempted, contact_viewed. entity_type VARCHAR(50) O Type of record affected, for example shipment or reservation. entity_id UUID O ID of the affected record. details JSONB O Event details such as QR result, OCR result, match outcome or failure reason. created_at TIMESTAMP R DEFAULT now() Time of the action.

docs.title: Backend deployment
docs.text: This page covers the backend only. Frontend deployment is documented separately in Frontend deployment, and AI reference-file operations in AI operations.

docs.title: Hosting and configuration
docs.text: Item Description Hosting Heroku hosts the ZamLine backend application. Database PostgreSQL. Database encryption is required. Secrets Database, routing, email and application secrets are retrieved from Vault. Secrets must not be stored in source code or client configuration. Transport security HTTPS and TLS protect all traffic to the backend API. Backups Backups are encrypted, access is restricted, and recovery access is separate. See Platform deployment.

docs.title: Release requirements
docs.text:
Before a backend release:

  1. Apply database migrations against the release database, with a recovery plan.
  2. Confirm production secrets are injected from the secret manager or protected deployment configuration, and are not printed during deployment.
  3. Verify HTTPS, CORS and allowed origins, cookie and session settings, error handling, health checks and audit events for the production domain.
  4. Run the smoke test described in the release checklist.

Development and production must differ in database, API URLs, secrets and debug configuration. Production errors must never expose internals.

docs.title: Backend security
docs.text: This page lists the security requirements for the backend modules: authentication and OTP, authorization, shipment and fleet management, matching and first-accept allocation, audit logging and error handling. Related pages: Business verification for uploads, Platform security for secrets, perimeter and database, and AI security for the Gemini integration.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Requirement Priority Every Shipper and Fleet Manager authenticates before reaching protected functions or organisation data High Email and password login, plus a short-lived, single-use email OTP with attempt and resend limits High Passwords are stored as hashes (users.password_hash) using a modern password-hashing algorithm High Secure session handling, with sessions ended on logout or expiry Medium

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Authorization is separate from authentication: it decides what an authenticated user may do.

Requirement Priority Role-based checks (shipper, fleet_manager) plus organisation-level checks High Users act only within their role and see only their organisation's data, or data exposed through the shipment workflow High Object and ownership checks on individual records High Organisation data isolation: one organisation's data is never reachable by another High Private cost data (the cost columns of companies, trucks.fuel_consumption_l_per_100km and trucks.maintenance_per_km) is returned only to the owning company High Only verified companies may post or accept shipments High Contact details are released only after a valid reservation High

docs.title: Input validation and error handling
docs.text: Requirement Priority Server-side validation of shipment weight, proposed payment, route inputs, fleet capacity and cost settings. Invalid, missing, negative or out-of-range values are rejected. High Database constraints enforce basic rules, for example weight_kg > 0, proposed_amount > 0 and latitude and longitude ranges. See Data model. High The Shipper confirms a shipment before it is published, and unaccepted cargo types are rejected High Error responses contain no stack traces, database details, credentials or internal paths Medium Failures of external services return controlled errors Medium

docs.title: Allocation integrity
docs.text:
Only one fleet company can secure a shipment. Two mechanisms enforce this:

  • The backend re-checks the shipment's state when a Fleet Manager accepts it.
  • reservations.shipment_id is UNIQUE, so the database rejects a second reservation for the same shipment even if two acceptances arrive at the same moment.

A successful acceptance creates the reservations row, sets the shipment to confirmed and sets the other matches for that shipment to closed. A Fleet Manager who loses the race receives a conflict response.

docs.title: Logging and monitoring
docs.text:
Requirement Priority Authentication events, verification results, shipment creation and material changes, fleet and cost-setting changes, acceptance outcomes and authorization failures are traceable Medium Logs exclude passwords, OTPs, tokens, API keys and unnecessary sensitive data Medium Audit logs have restricted access, integrity protection and retention controls High

The audit table and actions are described in Backend. The monitoring and alerting tools are not named in the project material.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: Integration Requirement Openrouteservice The API key is in the Vault, fetched only by the backend, and never exposed to the PWA, source code or logs. Failures return controlled errors. Only origin and destination coordinates and routing parameters are shared. Gemini API See AI security.

docs.title: Threats and required controls
docs.text: Threat Required control Unauthorized access Authentication, role-based access control, organisation-level authorization, server-side checks Cross-organisation data disclosure Organisation isolation and authorization testing Account compromise Secure session handling, safe account recovery, access monitoring Malicious or invalid input Server-side validation, accepted ranges, type checking, sanitisation Exposure of private cost information Organisation isolation, authorization, minimum necessary exposure Double shipment allocation Atomic allocation and concurrency testing Incorrect shipment details Required fields, range checks, Shipper confirmation before publication External routing failure Controlled errors, input validation, server-side key protection Sensitive information in logs A logging policy that excludes credentials, keys, tokens and unnecessary personal or commercial data

docs.title: Implementation standards
docs.text: Apply restrictive CORS rules, CSRF protection where cookie-based authentication is used, request throttling on authentication and OTP endpoints, a modern password-hashing algorithm, short-lived verification codes, pinned and scanned dependencies, parameterised database operations and context-aware output encoding. Keep configuration in the deployment environment and review it at every release.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text: The test framework, test locations and the command to run the suite are not documented here, and no test results or coverage figures are available. Add them to this page together with the backend's test configuration.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
These tests come from ZamLine's security requirements.

Test What it checks Source code review Authentication, authorization, business verification, cost handling and allocation logic API security testing OWASP Top 10 themes: authentication, authorization, IDOR and cross-organisation access, invalid input, error handling, rate limiting Organisation isolation Users from different organisations cannot reach each other's protected records Allocation concurrency Simultaneous acceptance by several Fleet Managers yields exactly one allocation External API failure Missing or invalid routing input, API authentication failures, unavailable service Dependency scanning Known vulnerabilities in third-party packages. Fix, replace or remove, then rescan. SAST Static analysis of the backend source where supported DAST Dynamic testing of the deployed test environment

docs.title: Verification and uploads
docs.text: Test Expected result Unsupported, corrupted, oversized or malformed certificate Fails safely with no crash, returns a controlled error and logs the attempt QR present but OCR mismatch Status is resubmit or rejected, never verified

docs.title: Recommended behaviour tests
docs.text:
These behaviours follow from the data model and business rules and are worth covering with named tests.

Behaviour Expected result Compatibility filter A truck matches when its body_type equals the shipment's required_body_type, its capacity_kg covers weight_kg, and it is available Verification gate Only verified companies can post or accept One reservation per shipment A second acceptance fails on the reservations.shipment_id uniqueness Match closure After acceptance, the other matches for the shipment become closed Contact visibility Contact details are hidden before reservation and visible after, and contact_viewed is logged Private cost fields Never returned to another organisation Data model constraints Positive weight and amount, coordinate ranges, unique plate number and registration number Error responses No stack traces, database details, credentials or internal paths

Cost and AI tests are in AI testing and evaluation. For the full test ownership matrix, see Testing overview.

docs.title: Business verification
docs.text: Business verification confirms that a company is registered before it can post or accept shipments. Both company types (shipper and fleet) verify with a PACRA certificate, which is the registration certificate issued by the Patents and Companies Registration Agency and carries a QR code. Only the storage link is kept in the database (companies.certificate_file_url). The file itself is held in separate storage.

docs.title: How verification works
docs.text:
Item Detail Input A PACRA QR-enabled certificate, uploaded as a file Checks File type and size, QR processing, OCR processing, and consistency rules between the QR and OCR results Result companies.verification_status: pending, verified, resubmit or rejected. resubmit means data is missing, unreadable or mismatched. Failure detail companies.verification_failure_reason, for example "QR not found" or "name mismatch" Timestamp companies.verified_at records when the company became verified Audit Every attempt is logged as verification_attempted, with the QR and OCR results in audit_logs.details Failure behaviour Verification fails safely when information cannot be reliably processed 
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> pending: registered
    pending --> verified: checks pass
    pending --> resubmit: unreadable, missing or mismatched
    pending --> rejected: checks fail
    resubmit --> pending: new certificate uploaded

docs.title: Security requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Priority Certificates are checked for file type and size. The upload limit is 10 MB. High QR and OCR processing fails safely and rejects when results are unreliable High Uploads are stored in controlled storage and processed safely, with restricted access to certificates High The QR and OCR consistency check uses deterministic rules and rejects safely High Threat Required control Unsafe file upload File type and size validation, controlled storage, safe processing Incorrect business verification QR and OCR consistency checks, deterministic rules, fail-safe rejection

Certificates are high-sensitivity data and may contain details of company representatives. See Privacy and retention.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Unsupported, corrupted, oversized and malformed certificates must fail safely. See Backend testing.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Certificate files are held in controlled storage separate from the database, and access is restricted to authorized verification workflows. See Backend deployment.

docs.title: Screens
docs.text: Registration includes the certificate upload area. A company that has not yet been verified sees a prompt to upload its PACRA certificate.

docs.title: Developer guide
docs.text:
This guide helps a developer find where to make a change and how to keep the documentation in step with it.

Page What it covers Testing overview Which component owns which required test Engineering standards Rules for security, workflow integrity, uploads and AI Release checklist The final gate before a production release

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
Setup instructions for the backend and the frontend are not documented here, because neither repository was available when this documentation was prepared. That includes prerequisites, installation, environment configuration, local services such as PostgreSQL and the secret manager, database setup and migrations, and the commands that run each application. Add them to the Backend and Frontend pages once they are confirmed.

Two procedures are documented and runnable:

  • Generating the cost-estimation reference files: see Running the notebook.
  • Building and previewing this documentation: see Building this documentation.

docs.title: Where to make changes
docs.text: Change Start from A table or column Data model. Update the migrations and that page together. Compatibility or matching rules The fleet matching module, described in Components and responsibilities Cost estimate behaviour AI Module, and the reference files via the notebook Acceptance behaviour First-accept allocation and the reservations constraints in Backend security Access rules The authorization module and Backend security A screen Pages and workflows

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• AI provider failure. Keep estimated_total_cost null and return a controlled message that the estimate could not be completed.
  • Failed Gemini file re-upload. Return a controlled error, log the operational event without credentials, and allow a safe retry. See Gemini file expiry and refresh.
  • Verification returns resubmit or rejected. Read companies.verification_failure_reason and the verification_attempted entry in audit_logs.details, which hold the QR and OCR results.

docs.title: Documentation conventions
docs.text: Rule Reason Update the documentation in the same change as the functionality Prevents drift Keep the documentation aligned with the implemented product and the approved requirements Keeps guidance consistent Never put real secrets, tokens, credentials or personal data in pages or screenshots Security Use real screenshots of the application, with private data removed Keeps pages accurate State plainly when a page does not cover a detail Readers can tell what is verified

docs.title: Building this documentation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.10 or newer. From the repository root:

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve --dev-addr 127.0.0.1:8002   # preview; choose any free port
mkdocs build --strict                    # fails on warnings, broken links or missing pages
./scripts/check_docs.sh                  # strict build plus image, placeholder and secret checks

The static site is written to site/. Publish the contents of that directory to any static host.

docs.title: Engineering standards
docs.text: These standards guide implementation, testing, deployment and day-to-day operation of ZamLine.

docs.title: Security and access
docs.text:
• Authenticate users before granting access to protected functions or organisation data.
  • Enforce role-based and organisation-level authorization on the server for every protected resource.
  • Validate request bodies, query parameters, uploaded files and business rules at the API boundary.
  • Store database credentials, external API keys and application secrets in the deployment secret store, and never expose them to the PWA or logs.
  • Return controlled errors without stack traces, SQL details, filesystem paths or secret values.
  • Keep audit events useful for investigation while excluding passwords, OTP values, session tokens, API keys and unnecessary personal data.

docs.title: Freight workflow integrity
docs.text:
• Re-check shipment eligibility when a Fleet Manager accepts an opportunity.
  • Process acceptance as a single-winner operation so a shipment cannot be allocated to multiple fleet companies.
  • Keep private fleet operating-cost settings within the owning organisation's access boundary.
  • Release contact information only within the permitted post-allocation workflow.
  • Present route and cost outputs as decision-support estimates, not guaranteed quotes.

docs.title: Business verification and uploads
docs.text:
• Enforce supported file types and the 10 MB upload-size limit on the server.
  • Process PACRA certificates in a controlled workflow, and restrict access to authorized verification operations.
  • Apply QR and OCR consistency rules, and fail safely when required information cannot be processed reliably.
  • Do not trust a client-provided filename or MIME type as the only basis for accepting an upload.

docs.title: AI and cost estimation
docs.text:
• Validate inputs before requesting an estimate.
  • Keep organisation-private operating costs out of responses to other organisations.
  • Handle provider errors with a controlled response, and never present a failed or incomplete result as a successful estimate.
  • Use deterministic test cases to verify arithmetic independently of generated explanations.
  • Keep reference-data provenance and model version information available for operational traceability.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text: Use this checklist as the final gate before a production release of the web application, API, database and AI cost-estimation service. Deployment procedures are documented separately for the backend, the frontend and the AI reference files.

docs.title: Application readiness
docs.text:
• [x] Shipper and Fleet Manager registration, login and email OTP flows work end to end.
  • [x] PACRA certificate upload, QR and OCR processing, verification result and resubmission paths behave safely.
  • [x] Shippers can create and manage shipments, and Fleet Managers can configure trucks and availability.
  • [x] Compatible shipment results respect fleet capacity, shipment status and organisation boundaries.
  • [x] Route distance and duration use the configured heavy-goods-vehicle routing profile.
  • [x] The cost assessment presents its assumptions and explanation clearly.
  • [x] Concurrent acceptance requests result in one allocation only.
  • [x] Contact details are revealed only after the permitted reservation state.
  • [x] Layouts, keyboard navigation, focus states and form error messages are usable on supported screen sizes.

docs.title: Security and privacy
docs.text:
• [x] HTTPS is enforced, and production secrets are injected from a secret manager or protected deployment configuration.
  • [x] No credentials, OTP values, tokens, private cost data or certificate contents appear in logs.
  • [x ] Role authorization and organisation isolation are tested for every protected resource family, including object-level authorization and IDOR scenarios.
  • [x] Upload validation rejects unsupported, malformed and oversized files.
  • [x] Rate limiting and safe error handling cover authentication, OTP and sensitive API routes.
  • [x] Dependency scanning and source security checks have been reviewed, and findings resolved or triaged.
  • [x] Audit events cover authentication, verification, shipment changes, fleet changes, cost assessment, allocation and authorization failures.
  • [x] Retention and deletion jobs follow the approved category-specific schedule and legal holds.

docs.title: Data and recovery
docs.text:
• [x] Database migrations complete successfully against the release database, with a recovery plan.
  • [x] A recent backup exists, and a restore has been exercised in a controlled environment.
  • [x] Database credentials have least-privilege access.
  • [x] Audit and business records remain consistent after a restart or a failed external request.

docs.title: AI and external services
docs.text:
• [x] Routing provider credentials are server-side only.
  • [x ] Gemini credentials are server-side only, and requests contain only the data required for estimation.
  • [x] Provider timeouts, invalid responses and rate limits produce controlled fallback behaviour.
  • [x] Cost outputs are checked against known deterministic scenarios, and historical references are labelled by period.
  • [x] Model and provider version and assessment metadata are retained for operational traceability.

docs.title: Deployment and observability
docs.text:
• [x] The production build succeeds, and static assets load from the configured domain.
  • [x] CORS, allowed origins, cookie and session settings and security headers match the production domain.
  • [x] Health checks, error monitoring and alert ownership are configured.
  • [x] Database and application logs are accessible to authorized operators only.
  • [x] Rollback and incident-response contacts are documented.
  • [x] A smoke test passes for the complete shipment lifecycle: registration, verification, shipment publication, fleet matching, cost assessment, acceptance and contact handoff.

docs.title: Testing overview
docs.text:
Each required test has an owning component. Details are on the component pages: Backend, AI, Frontend and Platform.

Test Backend AI Frontend Platform Source code review Yes Cost handling Authentication screens Secret handling Dependency scanning Yes Yes Yes SAST Yes Yes DAST Yes Yes Yes API security testing (OWASP themes) Yes Organisation isolation Yes File upload Yes (verification) Error display Allocation concurrency Yes Cost-calculation verification Yes External API failure Yes Yes Privacy review Yes Backup restoration Yes

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
The ZamLine frontend is a Progressive Web App (PWA) used by both Shippers and Fleet Managers. It is the interface through which users register, verify their business, publish and review shipments, manage fleets and decide on loads. It does not enforce permissions: the backend does, so hiding a screen is never a security control.

Page What it covers Pages and workflows The screens and step-by-step flows for each role Security Requirements that affect the PWA Testing Required and recommended frontend tests Deployment Frontend release requirements

docs.title: Pages by role
docs.text:
The sidebar of the signed-in application differs by role.

Role Pages Shipper Dashboard, Post Shipment, Current Shipments, Accepted Shipments, Profile Fleet Manager Overview, Opportunities, Booked Loads, Fleet Setup, Cost Settings, Cost Estimation, Profile

Before sign-in, the landing screen asks the user to continue as a Shipper or a Fleet Manager.

docs.title: Authentication screens
docs.text:
Users sign in with a business email and password, then confirm a one-time code sent by email. A "Forgot password?" link starts account recovery.

Registration and business verification are covered in Business verification.

docs.title: Technology
docs.text: The PWA's framework, routing, project structure, API base URL, request mechanism, state management, build tooling and hosting are not documented here, because the frontend repository was not available when this documentation was prepared. These pages describe the product behaviour that the screens show and the requirements the frontend must meet. Add the technology details to this page once they are confirmed.

docs.title: Frontend deployment
docs.text: This page covers the frontend only. Backend deployment is documented separately in Backend deployment.

docs.title: What is known
docs.text: Item Detail Client type A Progressive Web App for Shippers and Fleet Managers Entry path HTTPS and TLS, then DNS and DDoS protection, the WAF and the API gateway. The secure architecture diagram labels the WAF as provided by Vercel. Secrets No secret may be placed in client-side configuration. Configuration Keep environment-specific settings, such as the API base URL, outside committed source code.

docs.title: Release requirements
docs.text:
• Production builds succeed, and static assets load from the configured production domain.
  • The API base URL differs per environment and points at the matching backend.
  • The production domain and TLS certificate are configured before users are directed to the service.
  • A release updates the service worker and cache version so users do not keep stale assets, and the release procedure includes cache invalidation and a rollback path.
  • After release, a smoke test covers registration, verification, shipment publication, fleet matching, cost assessment, acceptance and contact handoff. See the release checklist.

docs.title: Requirements that affect the PWA
docs.text: Requirement Detail Secrets never reach the client External API credentials, database credentials and API keys stay out of source code, application files and client-side configuration. Transport Users reach the system over HTTPS and TLS. Authentication Email and password plus an email OTP. The PWA is where users enter them. Server-side validation Validation is required on the server for all listed fields. Client-side checks are not a substitute. Errors No stack traces, database details, credentials or internal paths are shown to users. Role and organisation visibility Users see only the screens and data that their role and organisation allow. Enforcement is in the backend, so hiding a screen is not a control. Uploads PACRA certificates are validated for type and size on the server. Security headers Apply HTTPS, a restrictive Content Security Policy and standard browser security headers at the web-serving layer and the API gateway. Privacy Driver location is not collected, and data is minimised to what the MVP needs.

docs.title: Threats and required controls
docs.text: Threat Required control Malicious or invalid input Server-side validation, accepted ranges, sanitisation (WAF and gateway) Account compromise Secure session handling, OTP, access monitoring Exposure of private cost information Backend organisation isolation. Never trust client-side filtering.

docs.title: Implementation standards
docs.text:
• Render user-supplied text as text, and encode output for its context to reduce cross-site scripting risk.
  • Apply a restrictive Content Security Policy and standard security headers at the web-serving layer.
  • Keep authentication material out of URLs, analytics events and application logs. Use the application's configured secure session mechanism and invalidate sessions on logout or expiry.
  • Configure service-worker caching so that authenticated responses and private organisation data are not stored in a shared or public cache.
  • Treat browser-side validation as a usability aid, and enforce business rules and authorization in the backend.
  • Keep the interface responsive and accessible, including visible focus states and readable colours in light and dark modes.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text: The frontend's test framework, test locations and commands are not documented here, and no test results are available. Add them to this page together with the frontend's test configuration.

docs.title: Required tests
docs.text:
These tests come from ZamLine's security requirements.

Test What it checks SAST Static analysis of the frontend source where supported Dependency scanning Known vulnerabilities in third-party packages DAST Dynamic testing of the deployed test environment, including the PWA Privacy review Only necessary data is collected, and driver location is not collected Source code review Review of where authentication and role-based screens are handled

docs.title: Recommended workflow tests
docs.text:
Workflow Expected result Registration and login with OTP A wrong or expired OTP is rejected, and attempt limits appear as an error PACRA upload An unsupported or oversized file shows a controlled error Post a shipment (Shipper) Required fields and ranges are enforced, and a confirmation step precedes publication Fleet setup Truck and cost settings are saved, and invalid values are rejected Opportunities (Fleet Manager) Only compatible open shipments are listed Accept or decline A second Fleet Manager sees a controlled failure if the load is already taken Contact handoff Contact details are absent before acceptance and present after Errors No internal details are displayed Role separation A Shipper cannot reach fleet screens, and the reverse. The backend must still enforce this.

Include installability, service-worker update, offline behaviour and low-connectivity scenarios in the PWA regression suite. Test on current supported desktop and mobile browsers and at responsive viewport sizes, and record the run, environment and outcome in the team's test record.

For the full test ownership matrix, see Testing overview.

docs.title: Pages and workflows
docs.text: This page walks through the main journey of each role, with screens from the application.

docs.title: Shipper
docs.text:
Workflow What happens Post a shipment The Shipper enters origin, destination, cargo type, weight, required body type, pickup time, special requirements and the proposed amount, and confirms before the shipment is published. Track status A shipment's status is open, confirmed, cancelled or expired. View the match and contact After a valid acceptance, the Shipper sees the accepting fleet company and its permitted contact details.

Dashboard. Summary counts and recent shipments.

Post a shipment. One form for route and cargo, and pickup and payment details.

Current shipments. The Shipper's published shipments and their status.

Accepted shipments. Shipments that a fleet company has secured, with the fleet company, agreed price, pickup time and status.

docs.title: Fleet Manager
docs.text:
Workflow What happens Fleet setup Add trucks with plate number, type, body type, capacity, fuel use, maintenance per km, availability and location. Cost settings Set private cost inputs: fuel price, driver allowance, tolls and other costs. These are visible only to the owning company. Opportunities See only open shipments that an available truck can carry, matched on body type and capacity. Cost estimation Review route distance and duration, the estimated costs, the margin against the proposed amount, the outcome and the explanation. Accept or decline Both decisions are stored. The first valid acceptance secures the shipment. Booked loads See the loads the company has secured, their status, and the shipper's contact details.

Overview. Opportunities ready to review, matched trucks and the cost settings status.

Fleet setup. Choose the truck types the company operates, then set the carrying capacity and availability of each truck in the fleet.

Selecting a truck opens its details, such as plate number, body type, capacity, fuel consumption and maintenance cost.

Cost settings. Private operating-cost inputs. The screen states that these values support the Fleet Manager's own review and never appear as public shipment information.

Opportunities. Compatible shipments with route, body type, weight, matched truck, pickup time and proposed payment.

Cost estimation. See AI Module for the cost estimation screen.

Booked loads. Each booked load shows its route, cargo, shipper, agreed price, pickup time and status (Active or Cancelled).

Booking details. After a booking, the Fleet Manager sees the shipper's business contact details and a booking reference. Contact details are available only in this post-allocation state.

docs.title: Cancelling a booking
docs.text: A Fleet Manager can cancel a booking and may give a reason. The confirmation dialog says that both companies' contact details are hidden again and that the action cannot be undone.

docs.title: Platform
docs.text:
The platform is everything the application runs on and behind: the perimeter, secrets, database, logs and backups.

Component Responsibilities Details DNS and DDoS protection DDoS mitigation, rate limiting Security WAF Input and output sanitisation, bot blocking, rate limiting Security API gateway Schema and body-size validation, rate, abuse and OTP throttling, security headers Security PostgreSQL (encrypted) Accounts, organisations, fleet, shipments, cargo, matches, reservations, private costs, audit records Security, Data model Secret manager (Vault) Database credentials, routing and email credentials, application secrets Security Audit and security logs Authentication, OTP, authorization, verification, cargo and allocation events Security Encrypted backups (Supabase) Restricted backup access, separate recovery access Deployment Page What it covers Configuration Configuration categories, secrets and environment differences Security Perimeter, secrets, database, logs, backups Testing Platform-level tests Deployment Hosting facts, backups and production release controls

Privacy, retention and compliance are in Security.

docs.title: Configuration categories
docs.text:
Configuration values differ between environments. Never place real values in documentation or source control.

Category Secret Notes Database connection Yes Held in the secret manager Routing service key Yes Never exposed to the PWA, source code or logs Gemini API key Yes A server-side secret Email (OTP) credentials Yes Held in the secret manager Application secrets, for example token signing Yes Held in the secret manager Public configuration, for example the API base URL No Set per environment outside committed source

docs.text: Component-specific deployment is documented separately: Backend, Frontend and AI operations. This page covers what they share.

docs.title: Backups and recovery
docs.text: Maintain encrypted backups with restricted backup access and separate recovery permissions. Set backup frequency and retention according to the operational recovery objectives. Test restoration before a production release and after material infrastructure changes.

docs.title: Production release controls
docs.text:
• Configure the production domain and TLS certificate before directing users to the service.
  • Use a repeatable deployment pipeline with a documented rollback path.
  • Configure health checks, structured logs and monitoring for the application and its dependencies.
  • Keep production secrets in the secret manager, and make sure they are not printed during deployment.
  • Do not scale the backend to several instances until the Gemini file registry is moved off the local server file.

docs.text: Layer Protections DNS and DDoS protection DDoS mitigation, rate limiting WAF Input and output sanitisation, bot blocking, rate limiting API gateway Schema and body-size validation, rate, abuse and OTP throttling, security headers

docs.text: Requirement Priority PostgreSQL is encrypted at rest, and data is protected in transit High Access is limited to authorised services with protected credentials High Private cost data is protected by organisation-level access control High Backups are secured Medium

docs.title: Logs and monitoring
docs.text: Audit and security logs record authentication, OTP, authorization, verification, cargo and allocation events, and exclude passwords, OTPs and keys. Audit logs require restricted access and integrity protection. Monitoring should alert on repeated authentication failures, authorization denials, verification anomalies, provider failures, allocation conflicts and unusual error rates. The monitoring and alerting tools are not named in the project material.

docs.title: Backups and recovery
docs.text: Application and audit records are backed up according to the chosen hosting and database environment, and recovery is tested before production. The secure architecture diagram shows encrypted backups on Supabase with restricted backup access and separate recovery access.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Project-specific terms and acronyms.

Term Meaning Shipper A person or business with cargo to be moved from point A to point B. Fleet Manager A person in charge of fleet operations in a logistics company. PACRA Patents and Companies Registration Agency, the Zambian agency for business registration, intellectual property registration and company records. API Application Programming Interface: rules that let software systems exchange data. QR Quick Response code, a two-dimensional barcode scanned to read stored information. OCR Optical Character Recognition: converting text in scans or images into machine-readable text. MVP Minimum Viable Product: the simplest working version with the main features. PWA Progressive Web App: a web application with app-like features such as installation and offline access. RBAC Role Based Access Control: access determined by a user's assigned role. HGV Heavy goods vehicle. The routing profile used for distance and duration. OTP One Time Password: a code that can be used once. 2FA Two Factor Authentication: two forms of verification before access. SAST Static Application Security Testing: examining source code for vulnerabilities without running it. DAST Dynamic Application Security Testing: testing a running application for vulnerabilities. IDOR Insecure Direct Object Reference: a user reaches another user's data by changing an identifier. OWASP Open Worldwide Application Security Project, a nonprofit providing security guidance and tools. ZDPA-2021 Zambia Data Protection Act, 2021. ZECTA-2021 Zambia Electronic Communications and Transactions Act, 2021. Openrouteservice The routing service used for distance and duration. Gemini Files API The API through which the Markdown reference files are uploaded for the Gemini model. Uploaded files expire. Reference files Markdown files, one per source document or dataset summary, given to the Gemini model as cost-estimation background. SCMS Supply Chain Management System: the USAID/PEPFAR delivery history behind the historical freight cost data. ZMW Currency code used in the reference files, for the Zambian kwacha. Allocation, reservation Both words describe a shipment being secured by a fleet company. The database table is reservations; the security requirements say allocation. Reservation (status) accepted when created, cancelled if called off. Shipment match A shipment and compatible truck pair holding route, cost estimate and the manager's decision. WAF Web Application Firewall: filters and sanitises web traffic before it reaches the application. Vault The secret manager that holds database, routing, email and application secrets. CORS Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: browser rules that control which sites may call the API.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: ZamLine handles business identities, commercially sensitive prices, private operating costs and contact details. This section shows where each security requirement is documented. The component pages contain the detailed requirements.

docs.title: Security by component
docs.text:
• Backend security

    Authentication, authorization, validation, allocation integrity, logging.

  • Business verification

    PACRA upload, QR and OCR checks, fail-safe behaviour.

  • AI security

    Data shared with Gemini, key handling, output boundaries.

  • Frontend security

    Secrets, sessions, errors and caching in the PWA.

  • Platform security

    Perimeter, Vault, database, backups.

  • Privacy and retention

    Sensitive data, third parties, retention, compliance.

docs.title: Incident response
docs.text: Treat suspected cross-organisation disclosure, incorrect shipment allocation, credential exposure and loss of audit data as priority incidents. Limit further exposure, preserve the relevant audit evidence, rotate affected secrets where necessary, restore service safely and record corrective actions.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
ZamLine collects only what the MVP needs: user names, business emails and contacts, account data, and verification documents that may contain details of company representatives. Driver-location data is deliberately not collected.

Area Requirement Purpose Data is used to create accounts, verify businesses, run shipment and fleet workflows, support communication between matched organisations and protect the platform. Data minimisation Collect only what the current MVP needs. Storage Personal, business and commercial data sit in the authorised ZamLine database with access controls. Secrets are kept in the Vault, never with normal application data. Access Access is limited by role and organisation. A Fleet Manager never sees another fleet company's private operating costs. A Shipper never receives a Fleet Manager's private cost calculations. Retention Periods are set per data category before production. See Data retention. Deletion Authorised deletion or anonymisation within 30 days of a verified request, keeping records that must be retained by law or operations.
