docs.title: Data retention
docs.text:
Retention is set per data category, not as one period for everything.

Data category Retention period After that User account and profile data While the account is active, then 30 days after termination Permanently deleted or anonymised unless the law requires retention Business profile and verification data While the business account is active, then 30 days after termination Deleted, except records under a legal retention requirement Completed load and delivery records 6 years after the transaction is completed Deleted or permanently anonymised Login and security audit logs 12 months Automatically deleted OTP and 2FA codes Until used or expired, at most 5 minutes Automatically invalidated and deleted Deletion requests 30-day grace period after the request is verified Personal data permanently erased, except legally retained records

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text:
• Zambia Data Protection Act, 2021: covers personal data such as account and business-contact information. Collect only what a defined purpose needs, protect it, and keep identifiable data no longer than necessary.
  • Zambia Electronic Communications and Transactions Act, 2021: where the law requires an electronic record to be kept, it must stay accessible, accurately represent the original and keep origin, destination, date and time information where required.
  • OWASP guidance: informs design, implementation and testing of the web application and API.

ZamLine’s implementation and operational processes must follow applicable legal obligations and the privacy controls on this page.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Zambia is a landlocked country that relies heavily on road freight to move goods through major regional trade corridors, including the North–South and Dar es Salaam corridors. These corridors are essential to domestic and international trade, but the sector continues to face high transport costs, delays and difficulty coordinating freight.

Operators must decide which vehicle should carry a load, what it can safely accommodate, when it should move, whether to wait for a return load or return empty, and what each option is likely to cost. Trip costing often means estimating fuel, driver expenses, accommodation, taxes and maintenance by hand. When vehicle details, shipment opportunities, route information and cost calculations are spread across tools or depend on individual experience, truck capacity may not be used efficiently. The result can be empty or partly loaded journeys, unnecessary kilometres, higher operating costs, higher fuel consumption and avoidable emissions.

How might we enable Zambian fleet operators to get more productive value from every truck journey while navigating real-world cost, route, timing and operational constraints?

docs.title: The solution
docs.text: ZamLine is a freight-matching and fleet-planning platform. It brings vehicle data, fleet requirements, shipment opportunities, route information and operating-cost estimates into one workflow so fleet operators can make better-informed decisions. ZamLine is decision support: the Fleet Manager decides whether to accept a load.

docs.title: Who uses it
docs.text:
User Role in ZamLine Shipper A person or business with cargo to move. Publishes shipments, tracks their status and receives the accepting fleet company's contact details after allocation. Fleet Manager The person in charge of fleet operations at a logistics company. Maintains trucks and private cost settings, reviews compatible shipments and cost estimates, and accepts or declines loads.

Both roles belong to a company, and both company types must pass PACRA business verification before they can post or accept shipments.

docs.title: How the workflow runs
docs.text:
1. Register and verify. Shippers and Fleet Managers register and submit a PACRA certificate for verification.
  2. Publish a shipment. A Shipper enters cargo details, origin, destination, pickup time, requirements and proposed payment.
  3. Maintain the fleet. A Fleet Manager keeps trucks, capacity, availability and private operating-cost settings up to date.
  4. Match and assess. The Fleet Manager reviews open shipments that available trucks can carry, with route distance, journey duration, estimated costs and margin.
  5. Accept or decline. A valid acceptance reserves the shipment for one fleet company. Other pending matches for that shipment are closed.
  6. Hand off. After allocation, each side can see the other's permitted business contact details.

The screens for each step are in Pages and workflows.

docs.title: What ZamLine does not do
docs.text:
• It does not collect driver location data.
  • It does not guarantee costs or profit. Cost estimates are indicative.
  • It does not release contact details or private cost settings before the rules in Security allow it.
